title: Concurrency vs. Throughput: why more parallelism can make databases slower — PlanetScale
excerpt: Increasing throughput sometimes requires reducing parallelism. A look into why this is the case for Vitess + MySQL databases
content_html:
Not long ago we watched a production MySQL database melt down for sixteen minutes.

The errors started as a trickle, a handful per minute, then fed on themselves:

minute   errors/min   queries/s
  0          5          15,000   <- a burst of work arrives
  2         60           3,900
  4        300           2,500
  6        550           2,000
  8        900           1,900
 10      1,400           1,500   <- error peak = throughput trough
 12        700           1,700
 14        250           2,000
 16          0           2,500   <- locks released, backlog drained
 18          0           8,500   <- full recovery, throughput jumps 5x

The trigger was fairly mundane: A batch job opened a transaction against a hot table, took row locks, and then held them for fifteen minutes without committing. A common application bug, the kind that eventually sneaks into many large codebases.

What happened around this long transaction is the interesting bit! The queries piling up behind that transaction were mostly not blocked on its locks at all. They were simple reads, where InnoDB didn't need to wait for row locks; it reads a consistent snapshot instead. Building that snapshot means walking back through the version history of every row the open transaction had touched, and that history grew for fifteen straight minutes.

This caused reads that normally took milliseconds to start blowing through their 90-second execution ceilings. The application retried them in a tight loop. Within minutes, more than ten thousand requests were piled up inside the storage engine. Processing each required reconstructing ever-longer version chains, and the resulting page reads outpaced the buffer pool's ability to free memory.

Now requests that had nothing to do with the locked rows, that touched entirely different tables, began failing too. The otherwise correctly sized buffer pool suddenly became too small to serve the crowd of queries.

At PlanetScale, we run our MySQL databases with Vitess, whose configured transaction timeout eventually killed the long-running transaction. Its locks were released, and the sixteen-minute backlog drained in about thirty seconds.

One slow transaction should not take down a database, and much of Vitess's plumbing is built around avoiding exactly this situation. So what went wrong? This was caused by the combination of the single long-running query and the ten thousand requests allowed in after.

Migration from Cloud SQL to Vitess

Some context on how a seemingly healthy database could end up like this in the first place.

This workload had recently been migrated onto PlanetScale from Cloud SQL, which ran Managed Connection Pooling, a thread-pool-style layer, in front of the database. A thread pool caps how many statements execute at once, commonly around a thousand, and queues the rest. A client arriving when the pool is full waits for a slot, usually for milliseconds, occasionally for a few hundred milliseconds. This cap can protect InnoDB's internals even under extreme load.

On PlanetScale, every MySQL shard sits behind a Vitess proxy called vttablet. These have a transaction pool, which caps how many transactions can be open against MySQL at once. Unlike a thread pool, when this pool fills, requests wait a set amount of time and then fail with an error.

For this workload, that small difference made the issue way worse. Errors propagated up an application stack that had never needed to handle them (since the Cloud SQL thread pool queued requests, pool-full errors effectively didn't exist there).

The solution that was initially tried was to raise the transaction pool cap and increase the timeout.

The pool was increased to ten thousand, a number chosen not by sizing but because it made the errors stop. However, this now limited Vitess's ability to control the backpressure between the application and the database storage engine.

Why high concurrency reduces MySQL throughput

Picture database transactions as items flowing down a conveyor belt (Factorio, anyone?). If they never interacted, throughput would scale in a straight line: twice the items in flight, twice the work done. That is the dream of a perfectly shared-nothing system, but rarely is that achieved. Somewhere on the belt there is a junction where multiple conveyor belts meet. In MySQL, this is the equivalent of a hot row, a latch, a CPU run queue, etc.

Below is a simple playground to visualize how request rate and queuing impact latency. Adjust the ARRIVALS / S slider to see the impact.

Little's Law describes this well. In steady state, N = X * W. Work-in-flight equals throughput times the time each request spends inside the database. Rearranged, X = N / W.

Adding in-flight requests raises throughput only as long as query execution time holds steady. If each new arrival stretches the execution/wait time of all the other queries within the database, the denominator now grows along with the numerator.

Just how badly can that go? Gunther's Universal Scalability Law splits the cost of concurrency into three terms:

                 γN
X(N) = ───────────────────────────
        1 + α(N−1) + βN(N−1)
  • N is how much work you allow to run at once.
  • γ is the ideal single-request throughput: the linear scaling coefficient if requests never interacted.
  • α (contention) is the cost of taking turns for a shared resource.
  • β (coherency) is the cost of requests making each other slower. Put differently, the work a database must do to keep shared state consistent across everything in flight.

Note the multiplier N(N−1), which grows with the number of pairs of requests. When N doubles, this coherency cost roughly quadruples.

Past a critical point, N_max = √((1−α)/β), β dominates, and total throughput actually starts to reverse. Gunther calls it retrograde scaling: beyond the peak, every request you admit requires coordination overhead and makes everything slower.

Let's look at how the problem from earlier maps to this equation. The row locks were α. The transactions that wanted those rows had to take turns, and no amount of concurrency changed the queue's drain rate. β, the real issue, was InnoDB trying to process so many queries at once: ten thousand concurrent snapshot reads, each made more expensive by the version history every other in-flight transaction was generating. The per-request cost rose with the increase in in-flight requests.

This is why focusing on "lock contention" does not explain the issue. The lock is just one of many potential junctions. It is the damage around the junction, the mutual slowdown of everything admitted past it, that scales with the square of concurrency and turns a slow batch job into a wider outage.

Reducing pool size and implementing queuing

To solve this, we implemented the reverse of the change that set this up, in both dimensions at once:

  1. Reduce the Vitess transaction pool size from ten thousand to roughly the thousand the old thread pool used. We now did this consciously and with evidence-backed proof: that workload had run successfully for years with a pool of that size.
  2. Instead of erroring after waiting, a transaction arriving at a full pool now queues for a slot with a longer timeout.

In other words, we configured Vitess's vttablet layer to mimic the old thread pool's behavior.

For this to be safe, two things must be true. The clients have to tolerate periodic waiting during bursts and the wait itself has to be bounded, so that a truly undersized system announces itself with timeouts at the queue rather than accumulating latency forever. Both are true for this workload.

The morning after rolling out this new configuration, it met its first test. A traffic burst arrived on a different Vitess shard of the same database, one that handles an order of magnitude more steady traffic. At peak, the pool handled around twenty-five thousand transaction pool slot requests per second against its thousand-odd available slots. Here are the results, in the same view we opened with:

minute   slot requests/s   errors/min   queries/s
  0             3,000           0         58,000
 10             9,000           0         61,000
 20            26,000           0         60,000   <- peak pressure, throughput flat
 30            17,000           0         59,000
 40             8,000           0         62,000
 50             4,000           0         60,000
 60             2,000           0         57,000   <- burst drained, queue empty

During the earlier incident, errors climbed to 1,400 a minute and throughput fell to a tenth of what the workload requested.

With the new and improved configuration, the application experienced no disruption and QPS didn't drop.

Over the entire day, database health was much better:

  • One rejected transaction. Despite slot requests/s at times jumping as high as 40,000, the queue absorbed effectively everything. Waits sat comfortably within the timeout.
  • Fewer than two hundred statements executing inside MySQL at any instant. InnoDB managed the bursts well. Sixty thousand queries a second through fewer than two hundred concurrent slots is Little's Law again: about three milliseconds apiece.
  • Lock contention didn't change. The hot-row pattern was just a minor contributor here. We were able to solve the problem without changing the lock contention dynamics.

This allowed the database to do less work at once, allowing it to do more work in total.

Below is another playground to visualize the difference between an open request flow and a gated one. Send bursts of traffic, simulate a locking event, and see the difference between a gated and ungated solution with the buttons below.

When to limit database concurrency

This is not a universal recommendation to tightly limit concurrency. Its applicability must be understood in the context of your workload.

  • Workloads built on pessimistic locking and contended shared state.
  • Hot rows updated by many workers.
  • SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on popular keys.
  • Long transactions holding locks while they do unrelated work.
  • Counters, balances, job queues.

If that describes your workload, added concurrency might just decrease your throughput!

The principles described here are not MySQL-specific. Postgres can have similar problems, but also a similar solution: PgBouncer's transaction pooling exists to allow for more client concurrency than server concurrency. This is why our Postgres offering comes with a local PgBouncer, and can be configured with dedicated primary and replica PgBouncer instances too.

Building systems that handle backpressure

Backpressure can't always be avoided, so make conscious choices about the expected behavior. The answer is almost never to simply raise a limit out of reach, but to fix what happens when that limit is reached.

Sometimes the fastest thing you can do for a busy system is to simply let less happen at once.

That is the dream of a perfectly shared-nothing system, but rarely is that achieved. Somewhere on the belt there is a junction where multiple conveyor belts meet. In MySQL, this is the equivalent of a hot row, a latch, a CPU run queue, etc.

sentences.en: Picture database transactions as items flowing down a conveyor belt (Factorio, anyone?).
sentences.zh: 将数据库事务想象成沿着传送带流动的项目（Factorio，有人吗？）。

sentences.en: If they never interacted, throughput would scale in a straight line: twice the items in flight, twice the work done.
sentences.zh: 如果它们从不交互，吞吐量将呈直线扩展：飞行中的物品是飞行中的物品的两倍，完成的工作量是完成的工作的两倍。

sentences.en: That is the dream of a perfectly shared-nothing system, but rarely is that achieved.
sentences.zh: 这是一个完美的无共享系统的梦想，但很少能实现。

sentences.en: Somewhere on the belt there is a junction where multiple conveyor belts meet.
sentences.zh: 传送带上的某处有一个交汇处，多个传送带在此交汇。

sentences.en: In MySQL, this is the equivalent of a hot row, a latch, a CPU run queue, etc.
sentences.zh: 在 MySQL 中，这相当于热行、锁存器、CPU 运行队列等。

blocks.html_en: Below is a simple playground to visualize how request rate and queuing impact latency. Adjust the ARRIVALS / S slider to see the impact.

sentences.en: Below is a simple playground to visualize how request rate and queuing impact latency.
sentences.zh: 下面是一个简单的游乐场，可以直观地看到请求率和队列如何影响延迟。

sentences.en: Adjust the ARRIVALS / S slider to see the impact.
sentences.zh: 调整 ARRIVALS / S 滑块以查看影响。

blocks.html_en: Little's Law describes this well. In steady state, N = X * W. Work-in-flight equals throughput times the time each request spends inside the database. Rearranged, X = N / W.

sentences.en: Little's Law describes this well.
sentences.zh: 利特尔定律很好地描述了这一点。

sentences.en: In steady state, N = X * W.
sentences.zh: 在稳定状态下，N = X * W。

sentences.en: Work-in-flight equals throughput times the time each request spends inside the database.
sentences.zh: 进行中工作等于吞吐量乘以每个请求在数据库内花费的时间。

sentences.en: Rearranged, X = N / W.
sentences.zh: 重新排列，X = N / W。

blocks.html_en: Adding in-flight requests raises throughput only as long as query execution time holds steady. If each new arrival stretches the execution/wait time of all the other queries within the database, the denominator now grows along with the numerator.

sentences.en: Adding in-flight requests raises throughput only as long as query execution time holds steady.
sentences.zh: 仅当查询执行时间保持稳定时，添加正在进行的请求才能提高吞吐量。

sentences.en: If each new arrival stretches the execution/wait time of all the other queries within the database, the denominator now grows along with the numerator.
sentences.zh: 如果每个新到达都会延长数据库中所有其他查询的执行/等待时间，则分母现在会随着分子一起增长。

blocks.html_en: Just how badly can that go? Gunther's Universal Scalability Law splits the cost of concurrency into three terms:

sentences.en: Just how badly can that go?
sentences.zh: 情况到底有多糟？

sentences.en: Gunther's Universal Scalability Law splits the cost of concurrency into three terms:
sentences.zh: Gunther 的通用可扩展性定律将并发成本分为三个方面：

blocks.html_en: • N is how much work you allow to run at once.

sentences.en: N is how much work you allow to run at once.
sentences.zh: N 是您允许同时运行的工作量。

blocks.html_en: • γ is the ideal single-request throughput: the linear scaling coefficient if requests never interacted.

sentences.en: γ is the ideal single-request throughput: the linear scaling coefficient if requests never interacted.
sentences.zh: γ 是理想的单请求吞吐量：如果请求从未交互，则为线性缩放系数。

blocks.html_en: • α (contention) is the cost of taking turns for a shared resource.

sentences.en: α (contention) is the cost of taking turns for a shared resource.
sentences.zh: α（争用）是轮流获取共享资源的成本。

blocks.html_en: • β (coherency) is the cost of requests making each other slower. Put differently, the work a database must do to keep shared state consistent across everything in flight.

sentences.en: β (coherency) is the cost of requests making each other slower.
sentences.zh: β（一致性）是请求彼此变慢的成本。

sentences.en: Put differently, the work a database must do to keep shared state consistent across everything in flight.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，数据库必须完成的工作才能在运行中的所有内容之间保持共享状态一致。

blocks.html_en: Note the multiplier N(N−1), which grows with the number of pairs of requests. When N doubles, this coherency cost roughly quadruples.

sentences.en: Note the multiplier N(N−1), which grows with the number of pairs of requests.
sentences.zh: 请注意乘数 N(N−1)，它随着请求对的数量而增长。

sentences.en: When N doubles, this coherency cost roughly quadruples.
sentences.zh: 当 N 加倍时，这种一致性成本大约增加四倍。

blocks.html_en: Past a critical point, N_max = √((1−α)/β), β dominates, and total throughput actually starts to reverse. Gunther calls it retrograde scaling: beyond the peak, every request you admit requires coordination overhead and makes everything slower.

sentences.en: Past a critical point, N_max = √((1−α)/β), β dominates, and total throughput actually starts to reverse.
sentences.zh: 过了临界点，N_max = √((1−α)/β)，β 占主导地位，总吞吐量实际上开始逆转。

sentences.en: Gunther calls it retrograde scaling: beyond the peak, every request you admit requires coordination overhead and makes everything slower.
sentences.zh: Gunther 将其称为逆行扩展：超出峰值后，您承认的每个请求都需要协调开销，并使一切变得更慢。

blocks.html_en: Let's look at how the problem from earlier maps to this equation. The row locks were α. The transactions that wanted those rows had to take turns, and no amount of concurrency changed the queue's drain rate. β, the real issue, was InnoDB trying to process so many queries at once: ten thousand concurrent snapshot reads, each made more expensive by the version history every other in-flight transaction was generating. The per-request cost rose with the increase in in-flight requests.

sentences.en: Let's look at how the problem from earlier maps to this equation.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看前面的问题如何映射到这个方程。

sentences.en: The row locks were α.
sentences.zh: 行锁是α。

sentences.en: The transactions that wanted those rows had to take turns, and no amount of concurrency changed the queue's drain rate. β, the real issue, was InnoDB trying to process so many queries at once: ten thousand concurrent snapshot reads, each made more expensive by the version history every other in-flight transaction was generating.
sentences.zh: 需要这些行的事务必须轮流进行，并且并发量不会改变队列的消耗率。 β，真正的问题是 InnoDB 试图同时处理如此多的查询：一万个并发快照读取，每个其他正在进行的事务生成的版本历史记录都使每个查询变得更加昂贵。

sentences.en: The per-request cost rose with the increase in in-flight requests.
sentences.zh: 随着飞行中请求的增加，每次请求的成本也随之增加。

blocks.html_en: This is why focusing on "lock contention" does not explain the issue. The lock is just one of many potential junctions. It is the damage around the junction, the mutual slowdown of everything admitted past it, that scales with the square of concurrency and turns a slow batch job into a wider outage.

sentences.en: This is why focusing on "lock contention" does not explain the issue.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么关注“锁争用”并不能解释问题。

sentences.en: The lock is just one of many potential junctions.
sentences.zh: 锁只是众多潜在连接点之一。

sentences.en: It is the damage around the junction, the mutual slowdown of everything admitted past it, that scales with the square of concurrency and turns a slow batch job into a wider outage.
sentences.zh: 交汇点周围的损坏，以及经过它的所有内容的相互减慢，与并发的平方成正比，并将缓慢的批处理作业变成更广泛的中断。

blocks.html_en: Reducing pool size and implementing queuing

sentences.en: Reducing pool size and implementing queuing
sentences.zh: 减少池大小并实施排队

blocks.html_en: To solve this, we implemented the reverse of the change that set this up, in both dimensions at once:

sentences.en: To solve this, we implemented the reverse of the change that set this up, in both dimensions at once:
sentences.zh: 为了解决这个问题，我们同时在两个维度上实施了与设置此更改相反的更改：

blocks.html_en: • Reduce the Vitess transaction pool size from ten thousand to roughly the thousand the old thread pool used. We now did this consciously and with evidence-backed proof: that workload had run successfully for years with a pool of that size.

sentences.en: Reduce the Vitess transaction pool size from ten thousand to roughly the thousand the old thread pool used.
sentences.zh: 将 Vitess 事务池大小从一万减少到旧线程池使用的大约千。

sentences.en: We now did this consciously and with evidence-backed proof: that workload had run successfully for years with a pool of that size.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们有意识地做到了这一点，并有证据支持：工作负载已经在如此规模的池中成功运行了多年。

blocks.html_en: • Instead of erroring after waiting, a transaction arriving at a full pool now queues for a slot with a longer timeout.

sentences.en: Instead of erroring after waiting, a transaction arriving at a full pool now queues for a slot with a longer timeout.
sentences.zh: 到达已满池的事务现在会排队等待超时时间较长的槽，而不是等待后出错。

blocks.html_en: In other words, we configured Vitess's vttablet layer to mimic the old thread pool's behavior.

sentences.en: In other words, we configured Vitess's vttablet layer to mimic the old thread pool's behavior.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们配置了 Vitess 的 vttablet 层来模仿旧线程池的行为。

blocks.html_en: For this to be safe, two things must be true. The clients have to tolerate periodic waiting during bursts and the wait itself has to be bounded, so that a truly undersized system announces itself with timeouts at the queue rather than accumulating latency forever. Both are true for this workload.

sentences.en: For this to be safe, two things must be true.
sentences.zh: 为了确保安全，有两件事必须是正确的。

sentences.en: The clients have to tolerate periodic waiting during bursts and the wait itself has to be bounded, so that a truly undersized system announces itself with timeouts at the queue rather than accumulating latency forever.
sentences.zh: 客户端必须容忍突发期间的周期性等待，并且等待本身必须受到限制，以便真正规模较小的系统在队列中通过超时来宣布自身，而不是永远累积延迟。

sentences.en: Both are true for this workload.
sentences.zh: 对于此工作负载来说，两者都是正确的。

blocks.html_en: The morning after rolling out this new configuration, it met its first test. A traffic burst arrived on a different Vitess shard of the same database, one that handles an order of magnitude more steady traffic. At peak, the pool handled around twenty-five thousand transaction pool slot requests per second against its thousand-odd available slots. Here are the results, in the same view we opened with:

sentences.en: The morning after rolling out this new configuration, it met its first test.
sentences.zh: 推出这一新配置的第二天早上，它就遇到了第一次测试。

sentences.en: A traffic burst arrived on a different Vitess shard of the same database, one that handles an order of magnitude more steady traffic.
sentences.zh: 流量爆发到达同一数据库的不同 Vitess 分片，该分片处理的流量要稳定一个数量级。

sentences.en: At peak, the pool handled around twenty-five thousand transaction pool slot requests per second against its thousand-odd available slots.
sentences.zh: 在高峰期，该池每秒处理大约 25000 个交易池槽位请求，并有 1000 多个可用槽位。

sentences.en: Here are the results, in the same view we opened with:
sentences.zh: 以下是结果，在我们打开的同一视图中：

blocks.html_en: During the earlier incident, errors climbed to 1,400 a minute and throughput fell to a tenth of what the workload requested.

sentences.en: During the earlier incident, errors climbed to 1,400 a minute and throughput fell to a tenth of what the workload requested.
sentences.zh: 在之前的事件中，错误攀升至每分钟 1,400 个，吞吐量下降至工作负载请求的十分之一。

blocks.html_en: With the new and improved configuration, the application experienced no disruption and QPS didn't drop.

sentences.en: With the new and improved configuration, the application experienced no disruption and QPS didn't drop.
sentences.zh: 通过新的和改进的配置，应用程序没有出现中断，QPS 也没有下降。

blocks.html_en: Over the entire day, database health was much better:

sentences.en: Over the entire day, database health was much better:
sentences.zh: 一整天，数据库的健康状况都好多了：

blocks.html_en: • One rejected transaction. Despite slot requests/s at times jumping as high as 40,000, the queue absorbed effectively everything. Waits sat comfortably within the timeout.

sentences.en: One rejected transaction.
sentences.zh: 一笔被拒绝的交易。

sentences.en: Despite slot requests/s at times jumping as high as 40,000, the queue absorbed effectively everything.
sentences.zh: 尽管槽请求/秒有时会跳至 40,000 个，但队列有效地吸收了所有内容。

sentences.en: Waits sat comfortably within the timeout.
sentences.zh: 暂停期间，等待表现得很舒服。

blocks.html_en: • Fewer than two hundred statements executing inside MySQL at any instant. InnoDB managed the bursts well. Sixty thousand queries a second through fewer than two hundred concurrent slots is Little's Law again: about three milliseconds apiece.

sentences.en: Fewer than two hundred statements executing inside MySQL at any instant.
sentences.zh: MySQL 中任何时刻执行的语句都少于两百条。

sentences.en: InnoDB managed the bursts well.
sentences.zh: InnoDB 很好地管理了突发。

sentences.en: Sixty thousand queries a second through fewer than two hundred concurrent slots is Little's Law again: about three milliseconds apiece.
sentences.zh: 每秒通过不到 200 个并发槽进行 60000 个查询，这又是利特尔定律：每个查询大约需要 3 毫秒。

blocks.html_en: • Lock contention didn't change. The hot-row pattern was just a minor contributor here. We were able to solve the problem without changing the lock contention dynamics.

sentences.en: Lock contention didn't change.
sentences.zh: 锁争用没有改变。

sentences.en: The hot-row pattern was just a minor contributor here.
sentences.zh: 热排模式只是其中的一个次要贡献者。

sentences.en: We were able to solve the problem without changing the lock contention dynamics.
sentences.zh: 我们能够在不改变锁争用动态的情况下解决这个问题。

blocks.html_en: This allowed the database to do less work at once, allowing it to do more work in total.

sentences.en: This allowed the database to do less work at once, allowing it to do more work in total.
sentences.zh: 这使得数据库可以一次性完成更少的工作，从而总共可以完成更多的工作。

blocks.html_en: Below is another playground to visualize the difference between an open request flow and a gated one. Send bursts of traffic, simulate a locking event, and see the difference between a gated and ungated solution with the buttons below.

sentences.en: Below is another playground to visualize the difference between an open request flow and a gated one.
sentences.zh: 下面是另一个可视化开放请求流和门控请求流之间差异的游乐场。

blocks.html_en: When to limit database concurrency

sentences.en: When to limit database concurrency
sentences.zh: 何时限制数据库并发

blocks.html_en: This is not a universal recommendation to tightly limit concurrency. Its applicability must be understood in the context of your workload.

sentences.en: This is not a universal recommendation to tightly limit concurrency.
sentences.zh: 这并不是严格限制并发的普遍建议。

sentences.en: Its applicability must be understood in the context of your workload.
sentences.zh: 必须根据您的工作负载来理解其适用性。

blocks.html_en: • Workloads built on pessimistic locking and contended shared state.

sentences.en: Workloads built on pessimistic locking and contended shared state.
sentences.zh: 基于悲观锁定和竞争共享状态构建的工作负载。

blocks.html_en: • Hot rows updated by many workers.

sentences.en: Hot rows updated by many workers.
sentences.zh: 许多工作人员更新了热门行。

blocks.html_en: • SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on popular keys.

sentences.en: SELECT ...
sentences.zh: 选择 ...

sentences.en: FOR UPDATE on popular keys.
sentences.zh: 有关流行按键的更新。

blocks.html_en: • Long transactions holding locks while they do unrelated work.

sentences.en: Long transactions holding locks while they do unrelated work.
sentences.zh: 长事务在执行不相关的工作时持有锁。

blocks.html_en: • Counters, balances, job queues.

sentences.en: Counters, balances, job queues.
sentences.zh: 计数器、余额、作业队列。

blocks.html_en: If that describes your workload, added concurrency might just decrease your throughput!

sentences.en: If that describes your workload, added concurrency might just decrease your throughput!
sentences.zh: 如果这描述了您的工作负载，那么增加的并发性可能只会降低您的吞吐量！

blocks.html_en: The principles described here are not MySQL-specific. Postgres can have similar problems, but also a similar solution: PgBouncer's transaction pooling exists to allow for more client concurrency than server concurrency. This is why our Postgres offering comes with a local PgBouncer, and can be configured with dedicated primary and replica PgBouncer instances too.

sentences.en: The principles described here are not MySQL-specific.
sentences.zh: 这里描述的原则并不是 MySQL 特有的。

sentences.en: Postgres can have similar problems, but also a similar solution: PgBouncer's transaction pooling exists to allow for more client concurrency than server concurrency.
sentences.zh: Postgres 可能有类似的问题，但也有类似的解决方案：PgBouncer 的事务池的存在是为了允许比服务器并发更多的客户端并发。

sentences.en: This is why our Postgres offering comes with a local PgBouncer, and can be configured with dedicated primary and replica PgBouncer instances too.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们的 Postgres 产品附带本地 PgBouncer，并且也可以配置专用的主 PgBouncer 实例和副本 PgBouncer 实例。

blocks.html_en: Building systems that handle backpressure

sentences.en: Building systems that handle backpressure
sentences.zh: 构建处理背压的系统

blocks.html_en: Backpressure can't always be avoided, so make conscious choices about the expected behavior. The answer is almost never to simply raise a limit out of reach, but to fix what happens when that limit is reached.

sentences.en: Backpressure can't always be avoided, so make conscious choices about the expected behavior.
sentences.zh: 背压无法总是避免，因此请对预期行为做出有意识的选择。

sentences.en: The answer is almost never to simply raise a limit out of reach, but to fix what happens when that limit is reached.

blocks.html_en: Sometimes the fastest thing you can do for a busy system is to simply let less happen at once.

sentences.en: Sometimes the fastest thing you can do for a busy system is to simply let less happen at once.
sentences.zh: 有时，对于繁忙的系统，您可以做的最快的事情就是简单地让更少的事情发生。

content_html_zh:
不久前，我们目睹了一个生产 MySQL 数据库崩溃了 16 分钟。

这些错误一开始是涓涓细流，每​​分钟几次，然后自行蔓延：

minute   errors/min   queries/s
  0          5          15,000   <- a burst of work arrives
  2         60           3,900
  4        300           2,500
  6        550           2,000
  8        900           1,900
 10      1,400           1,500   <- error peak = throughput trough
 12        700           1,700
 14        250           2,000
 16          0           2,500   <- locks released, backlog drained
 18          0           8,500   <- full recovery, throughput jumps 5x

触发器相当普通：批处理作业针对热表打开一个事务，获取行锁，然后将它们保留十五分钟而不提交。 一种常见的应用程序错误，最终会潜入许多大型代码库中。

围绕这笔漫长的交易发生的事情很有趣！ 该事务后面堆积的查询大多根本没有被其锁阻塞。 它们是简单的读取，InnoDB 不需要等待行锁；它改为读取一致的快照。 构建该快照意味着回溯开放事务所触及的每一​​行的版本历史记录，并且该历史记录连续十五分钟增长。

这导致通常需要几毫秒的读取才开始突破 90 秒的执行上限。 应用程序在紧密循环中重试它们。 几分钟之内，存储引擎内就堆积了超过一万个请求。 处理每个请求都需要重建更长的版本链，并且生成的页面读取速度超过了缓冲池释放内存的能力。

现在，与锁定行无关、涉及完全不同表的请求也开始失败。 原本大小正确的缓冲池突然变得太小，无法满足大量查询的需求。

在 PlanetScale，我们使用 Vitess 运行 MySQL 数据库，其配置的事务超时最终终止了长时间运行的事务。 它的锁被释放了，十六分钟的积压在大约三十秒内就被清空了。

一个缓慢的事务不应导致数据库崩溃，Vitess 的大部分管道都是围绕避免这种情况而构建的。 那么到底出了什么问题呢？ 这是由单个长时间运行的查询和之后允许的一万个请求相结合造成的。

从 Cloud SQL 迁移到 Vitess

首先，介绍一下看似健康的数据库如何最终会变成这样的背景。

该工作负载最近已从 Cloud SQL 迁移到 PlanetScale，后者在数据库前面运行托管连接池（一个线程池样式层）。 线程池限制一次执行的语句数量，通常约为一千个，并将其余语句排队。 当池已满时到达的客户端会等待一个槽，通常等待几毫秒，有时会等待几百毫秒。 即使在极端负载下，这个上限也可以保护 InnoDB 的内部结构。

在 PlanetScale 上，每个 MySQL 分片都位于名为 vttablet 的 Vitess 代理后面。 它们有一个事务池，它限制了可以同时针对 MySQL 打开的事务数。 与线程池不同，当该池填满时，请求会等待一段时间，然后因错误而失败。

对于这个工作负载，这个微小的差异使问题变得更糟。 错误会向上传播到从未需要处理它们的应用程序堆栈（由于 Cloud SQL 线程池对请求进行排队，因此实际上不存在池满错误）。

最初尝试的解决方案是提高交易池上限并增加超时时间。

池增加到一万，这个数字不是根据大小选择的，而是因为它可以阻止错误。 然而，这现在限制了 Vitess 控制应用程序和数据库存储引擎之间的背压的能力。

为什么高并发会降低MySQL吞吐量

将数据库事务想象成沿着传送带流动的项目（Factorio，有人吗？）。 如果它们从不交互，吞吐量将呈直线扩展：飞行中的物品是飞行中的物品的两倍，完成的工作量是完成的工作的两倍。 这是一个完美的无共享系统的梦想，但很少能实现。 传送带上的某处有一个交汇处，多个传送带在此交汇。 在 MySQL 中，这相当于热行、锁存器、CPU 运行队列等。

下面是一个简单的游乐场，可以直观地看到请求率和队列如何影响延迟。 调整 ARRIVALS / S 滑块以查看影响。

利特尔定律很好地描述了这一点。 在稳定状态下，N = X * W。 进行中工作等于吞吐量乘以每个请求在数据库内花费的时间。 重新排列，X = N / W。

仅当查询执行时间保持稳定时，添加正在进行的请求才能提高吞吐量。 如果每个新到达都会延长数据库中所有其他查询的执行/等待时间，则分母现在会随着分子一起增长。

情况到底有多糟？ Gunther 的通用可扩展性定律将并发成本分为三个方面：

                 γN
X(N) = ───────────────────────────
        1 + α(N−1) + βN(N−1)
  • N 是您允许同时运行的工作量。
  • γ 是理想的单请求吞吐量：如果请求从未交互，则为线性缩放系数。
  • α（争用）是轮流获取共享资源的成本。
  • β（一致性）是请求彼此变慢的成本。 换句话说，数据库必须完成的工作才能在运行中的所有内容之间保持共享状态一致。

请注意乘数 N(N−1)，它随着请求对的数量而增长。 当 N 加倍时，这种一致性成本大约增加四倍。

过了临界点，N_max = √((1−α)/β)，β 占主导地位，总吞吐量实际上开始逆转。 Gunther 将其称为逆行扩展：超出峰值后，您承认的每个请求都需要协调开销，并使一切变得更慢。

让我们看看前面的问题如何映射到这个方程。 行锁是α。 需要这些行的事务必须轮流进行，并且并发量不会改变队列的消耗率。 β，真正的问题是 InnoDB 试图同时处理如此多的查询：一万个并发快照读取，每个其他正在进行的事务生成的版本历史记录都使每个查询变得更加昂贵。 随着飞行中请求的增加，每次请求的成本也随之增加。

这就是为什么关注“锁争用”并不能解释问题。 锁只是众多潜在连接点之一。 交汇点周围的损坏，以及经过它的所有内容的相互减慢，与并发的平方成正比，并将缓慢的批处理作业变成更广泛的中断。

减少池大小并实施排队

为了解决这个问题，我们同时在两个维度上实施了与设置此更改相反的更改：

  1. 将 Vitess 事务池大小从一万减少到旧线程池使用的大约千。 现在，我们有意识地做到了这一点，并有证据支持：工作负载已经在如此规模的池中成功运行了多年。
  2. 到达已满池的事务现在会排队等待超时时间较长的槽，而不是等待后出错。

换句话说，我们配置了 Vitess 的 vttablet 层来模仿旧线程池的行为。

为了确保安全，有两件事必须是正确的。 客户端必须容忍突发期间的周期性等待，并且等待本身必须受到限制，以便真正规模较小的系统在队列中通过超时来宣布自身，而不是永远累积延迟。 对于此工作负载来说，两者都是正确的。

推出这一新配置的第二天早上，它就遇到了第一次测试。 流量爆发到达同一数据库的不同 Vitess 分片，该分片处理的流量要稳定一个数量级。 在高峰期，该池每秒处理大约 25000 个交易池槽位请求，并有 1000 多个可用槽位。 以下是结果，在我们打开的同一视图中：

minute   slot requests/s   errors/min   queries/s
  0             3,000           0         58,000
 10             9,000           0         61,000
 20            26,000           0         60,000   <- peak pressure, throughput flat
 30            17,000           0         59,000
 40             8,000           0         62,000
 50             4,000           0         60,000
 60             2,000           0         57,000   <- burst drained, queue empty

在之前的事件中，错误攀升至每分钟 1,400 个，吞吐量下降至工作负载请求的十分之一。

通过新的和改进的配置，应用程序没有出现中断，QPS 也没有下降。

一整天，数据库的健康状况都好多了：

  • 一笔被拒绝的交易。 尽管槽请求/秒有时会跳至 40,000 个，但队列有效地吸收了所有内容。 暂停期间，等待表现得很舒服。
  • MySQL 中任何时刻执行的语句都少于两百条。 InnoDB 很好地管理了突发。 每秒通过不到 200 个并发槽进行 60000 个查询，这又是利特尔定律：每个查询大约需要 3 毫秒。
  • 锁争用没有改变。 热排模式只是其中的一个次要贡献者。 我们能够在不改变锁争用动态的情况下解决这个问题。

这使得数据库可以一次性完成更少的工作，从而总共可以完成更多的工作。

何时限制数据库并发

这并不是严格限制并发的普遍建议。 必须根据您的工作负载来理解其适用性。

  • 基于悲观锁定和竞争共享状态构建的工作负载。
  • 许多工作人员更新了热门行。
  • 选择 ... 有关流行按键的更新。
  • 长事务在执行不相关的工作时持有锁。
  • 计数器、余额、作业队列。

如果这描述了您的工作负载，那么增加的并发性可能只会降低您的吞吐量！

这里描述的原则并不是 MySQL 特有的。 Postgres 可能有类似的问题，但也有类似的解决方案：PgBouncer 的事务池的存在是为了允许比服务器并发更多的客户端并发。 这就是为什么我们的 Postgres 产品附带本地 PgBouncer，并且也可以配置专用的主 PgBouncer 实例和副本 PgBouncer 实例。

构建处理背压的系统

背压无法总是避免，因此请对预期行为做出有意识的选择。 答案几乎从来不是简单地提高一个无法达到的限制，而是解决达到该限制时会发生的情况。

有时，对于繁忙的系统，您可以做的最快的事情就是简单地让更少的事情发生。
